item.title: Point Equivalence, Lie Symmetries, and Laurent Compatibility of the Time-Dependent Modified Dispersive Water-Wave System
item.description: arXiv:2611.33199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify local point transformations between members of the \((2+1)\)-dimensional modified dispersive water-wave class with two nowhere-zero real-analytic time-dependent coefficients. A change of time reduces the class to a single coefficient \(q\). An invertible differential substitution identifies this class with a slice of a previously classified coupled system and supplies a family of point maps. A direct calculation in the original field variables proves that the induced coefficient action \(\widetilde q(F(T))=q(T)/k\), with \(F'>0\) and \(k\ne0\) constant, exhausts all local point identifications. The order and relative sign of the first nonzero derivative classify nonconstant pointed coefficient germs. Constant germs admit arbitrary time generators, regular nonconstant germs admit one independent time generator modulo the zero-time-component subalgebra, and critical nonconstant germs admit none through the base time. On movable analytic hypersurfaces with \(\phi_x\phi_y\ne0\), the double-pole and regular-\(V\) Laurent branches both have an obstruction at resonance \(j=2\) proportional to \(q'\). Both branches are formally compatible exactly for constant \(q\), which is also the precise criterion for point equivalence to the standard system.
item.dc:creator: Manjit Singh

item.title: Point vortex dynamics influenced by the surface motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.33412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a coupled system of differential equations, which models the dynamics of fluid with a free surface and a point vortex in the body of the fluid. For long surface waves of small amplitude, the effects of the interaction between the waves and the point vortex are modeled within the framework of the Boussinesq regime. It turns out that the solitary waves on the surface are not destroyed by the interaction with the vortex, and, as a matter of fact, the solitary waves remain practically unaffected for a significant range of the vortex strength. As a result, a further simplification of the model is proposed, where the vortex motion under solitons propagating on the surface is determined from a system of decoupled ordinary differential equations.
item.dc:creator: Delia Ionescu-Kruse, Rossen I. Ivanov, Michail D. Todorov

item.title: Differential coupling drives Turing pattern formation in neural fields: a mechanism for Parkinson's disease and deep brain stimulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.33602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an effective treatment for the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet its mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. Abnormal beta-band synchronization in the basal ganglia and thalamocortical circuit is a hallmark of PD, but a theoretical framework linking network synchronization to spatial pattern formation is lacking. Here we show that a two-layer neural field model with differential interlayer coupling undergoes a Turing instability, spontaneously generating a diverse repertoire of spatially ordered patterns, including stripes, spots, rings, and spiral waves. The model yields the critical conditions and wavelengths for this instability, quantitatively predicting the observed pattern morphologies. Crucially, the interlayer difference, a natural measure of synchrony, exhibits strongly regime dependent dynamics. These findings establish a dynamical framework linking spatial pattern formation to pathological beta-band synchronization, providing a theoretical mechanism for DBS modulation of network states and a mathematical basis for optimizing stimulation parameters.
item.dc:creator: Ju Kang, Anmin Zheng

item.title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.34444v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.
item.dc:creator: Marcela C\'ardenas, Francisco Correa, Nicol\'as Salazar

item.title: Orbital Stability of Smooth Traveling Solitary Waves to the Fornberg-Whitham Equation
item.description: arXiv:2605.19906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Fornberg-Whitham (FW) equation was introduced by Fornberg and Whitham [Fornberg and Whitham, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A (1978)] as a nonlocal model for unidirectional shallow water waves capable of capturing wave steepening and breaking. Despite its similarities with integrable shallow-water equations, the FW equation is not completely integrable. Nevertheless, the FW equation is part of the family of peakon-type models as it supports peaked traveling wave solutions. In this paper, we consider smooth solitary wave solutions to the FW equation. We use a variational approach to show that some are orbitally stable.
item.dc:creator: Xijun Deng, Stephane Lafortune, Zhisu Liu

item.title: Dark and bright solitons in a multimodal lithium tantalate microresonator
item.description: arXiv:2611.30313v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bright-soliton and dark-pulse microcombs provide complementary outputs. Integrating both states in a single resonator would expand the operating capabilities of an integrated coherent source, but requires opposite group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) channels while reconciling localized interfamily interaction for dark-pulse formation with spectral isolation for independent bright-soliton pumping. Wavelength-addressed access to both states is achieved in a LiTaO$_3$ microring through two TE-like transverse mode families. The higher-order TE$_{10}$ family fulfills two distinct roles in different spectral regions. Within localized avoided-mode-crossing regions, mode-resolved spectroscopy implicates TE$_{10}$ in perturbing the normal-GVD TE$_{00}$ resonance sequence. Away from these regions, TE$_{10}$ retains anomalous GVD and remains spectrally isolated as an independently pumpable bright-soliton channel; at representative pump resonances, the closest resonance of the non-addressed family is separated by 75--192 loaded cavity linewidths. With the input polarization held fixed, pumping TE$_{00}$ and TE$_{10}$ resonances generates dark-pulse and bright-soliton microcombs, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first experimental realization of a dark-pulse microcomb in an integrated LiTaO$_3$ microring. These results establish transverse-mode-family engineering as a route to combining localized modal interaction with independent spectral addressing in a single microresonator.
item.dc:creator: Huizong Zhu, Yuyao Guo, Xiangfei Cheng, Yiqun Wu, Juanjuan Lu
